description: A 335-line program panics the compiler instead of compiling or reporting an error: 'index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0' at src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:1298 (develop 5b93e5fa9), in derive_runtime_demand_fact, at out.input_demands[index].join_assign(&demand) inside the loop over clause.params. A clause has parameters while out.input_demands is empty. Reproduces on every binary tried from cca160808 to 5b93e5fa9. Repro: fz2 interp /Users/j5n/Workspace/runtime-demand-panic-repro.fz (release build; the panic arrives after about 218 billion instructions, roughly 15 s, 394 MB peak, so the compile is also a runaway before it panics: the largest derivation set on one fact reaches 2,734 members). Not minimised. First step: minimise, then decide whether input_demands is sized from the wrong arity or the clause should not have reached this job.

comments.text: Duplicate of fz-sc8.140 (owned by the stack coordinator session, which has a five-line repro and the cause: an ActivationKey built from callable-surface inputs that include none, so input_len is 0 while the clause has params). /Users/j5n/Workspace/runtime-demand-panic-repro.fz is a second witness for that fix.

title: Deriving runtime demand indexes an empty input-demand list and panics the compiler
